title: Reconfigurable Microfluidic Channel with Pin-discretized Sidewalls
protocol: Degrease rectangular pins by immersion in acetone.
Immerse pins in 4 mL of 10% nitric acid and heat at 65 °C for 30 min in an oven.
Sonicate pins in deionized water for 5 min to remove residual acid.
Dry pins with a paper towel.
Immerse pins in 0.5 mL of mold release agent for 2 h.
Sonicate pins in deionized water for 5 min.
Draw or inscribe two parallel lines with a 4 mm gap on a glass slide using a ruler.
Apply chemical-resistant and low viscosity adhesive to one surface of two rectangular cut coverglasses.
Bond the two cut coverglasses on the glass slide at a 4 mm gap, using the parallel line as a guide.
Dispense two lines of silicone adhesive on the etching dish.
Put pins on the etching dish so that the 2 mm-long tips are immersed into the adhesive line pattern.
Dispense additional adhesive to ensure that the pins are completely covered and draw a contour.
Transfer the etching dish to a humidified fermenter heated to 38 °C.
Wait overnight to cure the adhesive.
Add 0.2 mL of 0.5 M nitric acid slowly to 0.2 mL of 5.0 M hydrochloric acid in a glass vial.
Put the etching dish on a hotplate heated to 65 °C.
Pour 0.4 mL of the acid mixture over the uncovered region of the pins.
Wait 10 min and transfer the acid to a beaker.
Neutralize all remaining acid, including the etched region of the pins, with 5 mL of 0.8 M sodium bicarbonate solution in deionized water.
Remove the pins from the etching dish by pulling them longitudinally with tweezers.
Sonicate the pins in deionized water for 5 min followed by sonication in acetone for 5 min.
Passivate the etched region of the pins.
Check the width of the etched pins with a shop microscope with a reticle.
Adjust the etching time so that the width of the etched region is 0.2 ± 0.02 mm.
Transfer the pins to a glass vial containing 5 ml of 70% ethanol.
Bring the vial to a laminar hood.
Pick up the pins out of the vial and allow them to dry.
Coat a degreased glass slide with 1 mL of negative epoxy photoresist using a spin coater at 1,000 rpm.
Dry the photoresist on a 95 °C hot plate for 15 min.
Repeat the coating and drying steps once.
Spin coat the third layer of the same photoresist at 2,000 rpm on the glass slide with coated photoresist.
Dry the photoresist on a 95 °C hotplate for 30 min.
Expose the photoresist layer to 450 mJ/cm² of 365-nm ultraviolet light from a UV spot light source through a photoplotted film.
Bake the exposed photoresist on a 95 °C hotplate for 15 min.
Develop the photoresist by spraying a solvent (2-methoxy-1-methylethyl acetate) using a hand sprayer.
Blow-dry the developed photoresist with nitrogen gas.
Pour prepolymer of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) onto the mold to a thickness of 3 mm.
Debubble the PDMS prepolymer in a vacuum desiccator at -800 kPa for 10 min.
Cure the PDMS prepolymer in an oven at 65 °C for 1 h.
Demold the partially cured PDMS slab using a scalpel.
Fully cure the PDMS in an oven at 120°C for 1 h.
Trim away irregular edges from the PDMS slab with the same scalpel along the guideline pattern.
Make as precise and clean a cut as possible, particularly at the surface that defines the insertion slot.
Perforate 2 mm-diameter holes for inlet/outlet into the ends of the main channel using biopsy punches.
Perforate 1 mm-diameter holes at the ends of the air vent channel using biopsy punches.
Immerse a 10 × 20 mm No. 4 coverglass in a cleaning solution heated to 60 °C for 10 min.
Rinse the coverglasses with deionized water twice.
Dry the coverglasses at 120 °C for 10 min.
Place the PDMS slab and cleaned coverglass in the vacuum chamber of a sputter coater.
Start pumping down the chamber to 60 Pa.
Generate air vacuum plasma (20 mA) for 30 s.
Immediately vent the chamber.
Bond the channel feature side of the PDMS slab to the coverglass with their edges aligned.
Place the bonded layers in a 65 °C oven for 10 min.
Bring the bonded layers to a laminar hood using a sterile container.
Sterilize the bonded layers with UV light for 30 min.
Insert pins into the slot so that their ends form the other sidewall of the microchannel.
Ensure adjacent pins are different in length to avoid contact between vertical ends.
Make or read a part file of the base using CAD/CAM software.
Create two numerical control (NC) files containing toolpaths for machining.
Install a 4 mm end mill to the CNC mill.
Locate part zero by touching the end mill to the PMMA board.
Run the first NC code to cut the board.
Occasionally blow the end mill tip with compressed air during cutting.
Repeat steps using the second NC file and a 1 mm end mill.
Degrease the machined parts with detergent.
Dry the degreased parts with a paper towel.
Spray the parts with 70% ethanol.
Prepare gap filler by mixing white petrolatum and polytetrafluoroethylene powder at a 2:1 ratio by weight.
Homogenize the mixture using an ultrasonic homogenizer.
Pour the gap filler into a dispenser syringe.
Insert a plunger into the filled syringe tip.
Push the plunger until the needle tip is filled with gap filler.
Likewise, prepare a dispenser syringe with a plunger and a needle filled with silicone adhesive.
Connect each syringe to a pneumatic dispenser using an adapter tube.
Adjust the dispense pressures for silicone adhesive and filler to 250 kPa and 280 kPa.
Dispense silicone adhesive to the edge of a pocket of the base.
Place a 10 × 20 mm No.4 coverglass on the pocket and press it firmly to bond.
Dispense silicone adhesive to a depth of approximately 1 mm to draw two segments along two outer slots of the base.
Dispense gap filler to a depth of approximately 1 mm, to draw segments along the other slot.
Dispense silicone adhesive to the edge of another pocket.
Place a microchannel assembly on the pocket and press it firmly to bond.
Repeat bonding steps to ensure that both gap filler and silicone adhesive fully embed the pins and that there is no opening at the slots.
Put the device in a sterile container such as a stainless steel box with lid.
Transfer the container to a humidified fermenter heated to 38 °C.
In the laminar hood, cure the elastomeric barrier for one day.
Move each pin up to 1 mm along adjacent pins to release the pins from the cured elastomeric barrier.
Sterilize the device with UV light for 30 min.
Detect leakage using fluorescence.
Open the microchannel using a fine tool or a desktop robot.
Make the channel width as consistent throughout the channel as possible.
Dilute a green fluorescent dye with deionized water at 10 µM to make fluorescence solution.
Add fluorescence solution to one of the end ports of the microchannel with a micropipettor.
Put the microfluidic device and two pieces of absorbent paper wet with deionized water in a large plastic dish.
Incubate the dish at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for at least 24 h.
Record green fluorescence images of the microchannel with an inverted fluorescent microscope using a microscope camera.
Open the fluorescent images with appropriate image analysis software.
Confirm there is no leakage (green fluorescence) at the interface of the gap filler and the pins.
Prepare a cell culture vessel containing 70 - 80% confluent cells depending on cell types.
Detach and suspend the cells in growth medium.
Centrifuge the cells, speed and time depend on cell types.
Aspirate the medium.
Resuspend the cells with a small amount of medium.
Count the cells with a cell counter.
Adjust the cell density from 1.5 × 106 to 1.5 × 107 cells/mL.
Open the microchannel using a fine tool or a desktop robot to make a straight 400-µm-wide channel.
Adjust pin positions to make the sidewall as flat throughout the channel as possible.
Add cell suspension to one of the end ports of the microchannel and fill the channel.
Locate one of the pins that defines the sidewall of the region to start culture.
Under an inverted microscope, close the two adjacent pins to enclose cells in the cell culture region.
Close all pins from inner to outer to expel all cells from the channel.
Gently aspirate suspension from the end ports.
Add medium to the end ports.
Incubate the device as described in 4.1.4.
When cells are about 70 - 80% confluent, slowly open a pin to widen the culture area.
